subject: AcmeTech AWS Private Offer — special rev-share / SLA carveouts (exec clearance needed)
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@acmetech.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private offer proposal — early rev-share tilt + onboarding credit

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. We're excited to move fast — AcmeTech is ready to list Redwood on our AWS private offer, but procurement and finance require a couple of commercial concessions to close this quarter. Summary of asks: 

- Rev-share: 85/15 to AcmeTech for months 0–12 (then reverts to standard 70/30).
- Onboarding credit: one-time $120k credit applied at invoice for month 1.
- Payment terms: net-60.
- SLA: request 99.5% uptime commitment for our listed private offer; we need an exception for marketplace listing.
- Usage carveout: for any single-customer month > $1.2M, AcmeTech wants to invoice that overage directly to Redwood at list price (we tag as resale).

I've attached our proposed contract language and a short procurement memo. Can you route to your deal desk and legal — we need a signed private offer by Dec 8 to hit our internal vendor listing window.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Park
Head of Cloud Partnerships, AcmeTech
[Attachment: AcmeTech_Private_Offer_Draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 142KB)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Private offer proposal — early rev-share tilt + onboarding credit

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in. Potential $2.8M ACV over first 12 months if we accept the 85/15 rev-share and the onboarding credit. The buyer is pushing hard on timeline (wants signed PO by Dec 8).

Key risk items for approval:
- Rev-share at 85/15 months 0–12 (material economics impact).
- One-time onboarding credit $120k.
- SLA exception to 99.5% for AWS private listing (our standard marketplace SLA is 99.0%/month).
- Net-60 + usage carveout above $1.2M/month (commercially unusual).

Attachments: AcmeTech draft + our internal sandbox of typical AWS private-offer clauses.

Ask: Marissa — what's Deal Desk recommendation (approve as-is vs counter)? Karthik — any immediate legal redlines we should push back on before taking to Laura for executive clearance? Laura — if Deal Desk recommends, can you review and provide exec sign-off? This is a named anchor customer in our Q4 target.

Thanks,
Connor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment forwarded: AcmeTech_Private_Offer_Draft_v1.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T11:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer proposal — Deal Desk recommendation + ask for exec clearance

Connor — thanks for the context and numbers. Quick Deal Desk read: 

Recommendation (short): proceed with an approval play that balances customer momentum and unit economics. Proposed carve to present for exec sign-off: 

1) Rev-share: approve 80/20 to AcmeTech for months 0–6, then 70/30 months 7–12, revert to standard thereafter.
2) Onboarding credit: approve $80k (one-time) instead of $120k — applied as a contra invoice over first two invoices.
3) Payment terms: net-60 OK for first 6 months; require auto-switch to net-30 after month 6 if utilization stays under $900k/mo.
4) SLA: cannot change platform SLA blanket; can offer a marketplace-level addendum that includes a 99.5% target for the listing page only, with a capped SLA credit schedule. Legal will need to limit operational exposure.
5) Usage carveout: propose a threshold-based approach — for months > $1.2M, revenue above threshold will be billed through standard Redwood terms (not direct invoicing). We should avoid reseller carveouts.

Attachments: internal impact memo and a short terms summary (rwrd-sla-exception-memo.docx). Please review and if we agree, this will need Laura's executive clearance for the rev-share delta + SLA exception.

Marissa
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rwrd-sla-exception-memo.docx (DOCX, 48KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer proposal — Legal redlines and gating items

All,

I reviewed Acme's draft and Marissa's proposed commercial carve. Legal ok on principle with the 80/20 (0–6) then 70/30 (7–12) tier structure, subject to the following binding redlines we must include before exec sign-off: 

- Explicit liability cap: limit to fees paid in prior 12 months (no broader operational indemnity).
- SLA addendum must include a maximum aggregate credit exposure of 2% of invoiced value per quarter.
- No third-party resale/invoicing: remove wording that allows AcmeTech to invoice overage directly — instead include a passthrough reporting requirement and an escalation path for large monthly overages; any alternative billing flow must be implemented via a separate commercial agreement.
- Termination for convenience: require 60-day notice and pro-rated credit for unused onboarding credit.

If Marissa and Connor accept, we can prepare an internal executive memo and a one-page signoff. Laura — this is the commercial ask that will require your sign-off for the rev-share and SLA credit cap.

-Karthik
Head of Marketplace Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T17:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer proposal — Exec clearance (ACME-2028-AWS-PO-0921)

Thanks team — I reviewed Deal Desk and Legal recommendations. Executive decision: approve the proposed compromise with the following firm conditions (non-negotiable):

1) Economics: accept 80/20 for months 0–6 and 70/30 for months 7–12; after month 12 revert to company standard. No further retroactive discounts.
2) Onboarding credit: authorize $80k, applied as a contra across first two invoices; must be clawed back pro rata on early termination.
3) Payment terms: net-60 for first six months only; after month 6 auto-switch to net-30 unless senior finance exec waiver is submitted.
4) SLA: approve a marketplace-specific addendum with 99.5% target but cap total SLA credits at 2% quarterly. All SLA language must be approved by Legal before signature.
5) No direct resale invoicing by AcmeTech. Any special billing arrangement requires a separate signed MSA amendment reviewed by Finance.

Connor — you have executive clearance to present these terms to AcmeTech and finalize the attached one-page signoff. Get procurement to initial the one-pager and send DocuSign. If they push for the original 85/15 or $120k credit, decline and present the approved compromise.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — North America, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Exec_Clearance_AcmeTech_2028-11-29.pdf (PDF, 12KB)]
